body_long:
The Chancery Rosewood, the hotel in the former US Embassy on Grosvenor Square, has appointed Boris Messmer as Managing Director. He takes up the post on 1 February 2027 and succeeds Michael Bonsor, who has led the hotel since 2023 and will take on a new role within Rosewood. The owner, Qatari Diar, announced the appointment on 12 November 2026.

## A London career

Messmer's path runs through the capital's grandest addresses. He worked at The Dorchester and was part of the reopening team at The Savoy, after a period at the Fairmont Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten in Hamburg. In 2015 he joined Maybourne as Front of House Manager at Claridge's, then became Director of Rooms before serving as Hotel Manager at The Berkeley and The Connaught.

## From the Riviera to Frankfurt

In 2021 he was appointed General Manager of The Maybourne Riviera and led the opening of the group's first property in France, on the Côte d'Azur. In 2024 he moved to Germany as General Manager of The Florentin, part of the Althoff Collection in Frankfurt. The Caterer describes the new role as his return to the London luxury scene after five years.

## The hotel

The Chancery Rosewood opened on 1 September 2025 in the Grade II-listed former US Embassy, after a £1bn redevelopment financed by Qatari Diar. The architectural restoration was led by David Chipperfield, with interiors by Joseph Dirand. The hotel counts 144 suites, eight restaurants and bars, an Asaya spa and event spaces. Messmer says he is "immensely proud" to join and looks forward to "inspiring our people".

## The signal

London's newest landmark hotels are recruiting from its oldest. A career shaped at Claridge's, The Berkeley and The Connaught, followed by an opening abroad, has become the profile owners look for when a young hotel moves from launch to its second chapter.

Congratulations to Boris Messmer on his new role.
summary: The former opening general manager of The Maybourne Riviera becomes Managing Director of The Chancery Rosewood on Grosvenor Square from 1 February 2027, succeeding Michael Bonsor.
